title: RBAC & Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Compliance Evidence, and Risk Exceptions
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's operational security and compliance controls for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security), compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for service owners, platform engineers, security reviewers, and auditors.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control planes, and Private deployments where Redwood provides operational tooling or support.
- Excludes low-risk marketing content and public-facing documentation unless explicitly referenced.

Owners and escalation
- Primary owner: Security team (security@redwood.com).
- Secondary owners: Eng-Platform and Eng-Infra (service-specific).
- Audit and evidence owner for SOC2/ISO: Compliance Engineering (compliance@redwood.com).

Principles
- Least privilege: default-deny RBAC, minimize blast radius, use roles not user-specific policies.
- Defense in depth: combine strong auth, tenant isolation, network controls, and monitoring.
- Evidence-first: instrument systems to produce auditable artifacts automatically.
- Time-bound exceptions: temporary compensating controls approved and tracked.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Summary
Redwood uses a role-based access control (RBAC) model across identity providers (IdP) and internal services. Primary IdP: Okta (SAML + SCIM). Service-level short-lived credentials issued via our gateway (redwood-auth).

Roles and role examples
- org-admin: company-wide administrative tasks (restricted to named employees).
- security-admin: manage detection, response, and security policy objects.
- infra-engineer: cluster, network, and capacity operations (no customer data access by default).
- service-owner: owner for a specific service (deploys, config, runtime keys).
- developer: CI/CD and code-level deployment roles with limited runtime access.

RBAC rules and requirements
- All service access must be routed via redwood-auth or Okta short-lived role sessions.
- No hard-coded long-lived credentials in source repositories. CI uses vault-agent to fetch ephemeral tokens.
- Access reviews: quarterly review for org-admin and security-admin roles; semi-annual for infra-engineer and service-owner roles.
- Just-in-time (JIT) privileged access: use Okta MFA + approval workflow for elevation; maximum 8-hour session for elevated roles.

Authentication and MFA
- MFA required for all interactive accounts (Okta MFA: TOTP and hardware token allowed).
- SSO enforced for contractors; SCIM provisioning used for automated deprovisioning.

Change control and onboarding
1. Request access via Access Request form (Confluence link available on team pages).
2. Manager + service-owner approval required for production roles.
3. Create time-bound access (maximum 90 days) unless exception granted.
4. Onboarding tasks: training sign-off, accept data handling policy, and sign NDA when applicable.

2) Audit Logging
Goals
- Maintain an immutable, searchable record of security-relevant events to support detection, investigation, and compliance audits.

What is logged
- Identity events: SSO logins, MFA failures, SAML assertions, SCIM provisioning events.
- Privilege events: role grants/revokes, JIT elevations, admin actions.
- Infrastructure events: instance launches/terminations, network ACL changes.
- Application events: model version deployments, key rotations, encryption configuration changes.
- Data access events: access to customer data stores, exports, backups.

Log pipeline and retention
- Agents forward logs to the central logging cluster (Splunk for security logs; Datadog for operational traces).
- Primary hot retention: 1 year (fast search).
- Long-term cold archive: 7 years in encrypted S3 (glacier-class policy for compliance evidence).
- Critical audit logs (authentication, privilege changes, data exports): retained 7 years immutable.

SLOs and monitoring
- Logging availability SLO: 99.9% (logs accepted by central pipeline).
- Alerting: missing heartbeat or log gaps >5 minutes for critical services triggers P1.
- Integrity checks: weekly digest signed and stored in compliance-bucket (owner: Compliance Engineering).

3) Data Residency & Retention
Residency model
- Redwood supports region-specific deployments. Default hosted regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1.
- Customer deployments can be pinned to a region in contract (region guarantee included in Dedicated and Private).

Classification and handling
- Data classification levels: public, internal, confidential, regulated.
- Regulated data (e.g., PII, payment identifiers) must be stored in contracted region and use encryption-at-rest (KMS) and in-transit (TLS1.2+).

Retention policy (summary table)
| Artifact                      | Hot retention | Archive retention | Owner |
|-------------------------------|---------------|-------------------|-------|
| Authentication logs           | 1 year        | 7 years           | Security |
| Application traces            | 90 days       | 1 year            | Eng-Platform |
| Backups (customer data)       | 90 days       | Per contract (min 1 year) | Customer Success |
| Audit artifacts (SOC2 evidence)| 7 years       | 7 years           | Compliance Engineering |

Data deletion and egress
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) process. Standard DSR SLA: 30 days.
- When a contract requires data egress or deletion on termination, follow the Contract Exit Checklist and generate an egress plan owned by Customer Success + Eng-Infra.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)
Mandatory gates
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST) on pull requests, fail on high/critical issues.
- Dependency scanning (SCA) on every release; high-severity CVEs must be remediated or mitigated with documented compensating controls.
- Secrets scanning in PRs and CI; any leaked secrets must follow the secret-rotation runbook immediately.
- Mandatory code review by at least one owner and one security reviewer for services handling confidential/regulatory data.

Release controls
- CI pipelines must produce build artifacts signed with the build-signing key (stored in HSM/KMS).
- Canary and progressive rollouts via Redwood Console: default canary 5% for 30 minutes, automatic rollback on error rate >1% or latency SLO breach (see Performance Standards).

Threat modeling and design review
- New services and major changes require a lightweight threat model (MITRE ATT&CK mapping) and an architecture design review with Security.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Incident classification
- Sev P0 (Breach / data exfiltration impacting >1 customer or regulated data)
- Sev P1 (Service compromise or vulnerability with high likelihood exploit)
- Sev P2 (Partial service outage, limited blast radius)
- Sev P3 (Minor security issues and information requests)

Immediate steps (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage and classification: Incident lead (oncall security) assigns severity and documents timeline.
2. Containment: apply short-term controls (network block, role revokes, key rotation).
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot affected instances, preserve logs (immutably), capture disk images if forensic analysis needed.
4. Notify stakeholders: Security, Eng-Infra, Legal, CS, and assigned service-owner.

Investigation and forensics
- All forensic actions must follow chain-of-custody templates and be logged in the incident ticket. Use designated forensic VMs and approved tools.
- For incidents involving customer data, notify Legal and Compliance within 2 hours.

Public disclosure and legal obligations
- For material data breaches, follow the external notification timeline: notify affected customers within 72 hours where required (GDPR) and execute the legal-approved communications plan.

Post-incident actions
- Postmortem within 72 hours for P0/P1; public (internal) postmortem published in Confluence with root cause, timeline, remediation, and action owners.
- Track remediation in the security backlog until verified.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Audit readiness (SOC2 / ISO27001)
- Evidence owners per control must maintain one-click exports: configuration snapshots, access review artifacts, signed change requests, and log digests.
- Primary evidence storage: encrypted compliance-bucket (S3) with restricted access via IAM role (read-only to auditors for the duration of the audit).

Typical evidence package contents
- Control mapping spreadsheet (control -> artifact IDs).
- System design diagrams and threat models.
- Access review reports and separation-of-duty attestations.
- Immutable log digests and signed retention manifests.

Evidence collection process (step-by-step)
1. Compliance requests evidence via audit ticket.
2. Evidence owner gathers artifacts, validates signatures, and uploads to compliance-bucket with manifest.
3. Compliance Engineering reviews and timestamps the package.
4. Auditor access is granted to a time-bound, read-only role and logged.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process
Risk register and approvals
- All exceptions must be recorded in the Security Exceptions Register (Confluence table + Jira ticket).
- Exceptions are reviewed weekly by the Risk Review Board (RRB): Security lead, Eng-Platform lead, and Compliance Engineering.

Exception lifecycle
1. Submit exception request with: business justification, risk assessment (likelihood x impact), compensating controls, expiration date (max 90 days), and rollback plan.
2. RRB evaluates and either: approve, conditionally approve (with controls), or deny.
3. Approved exceptions auto-escalate if not remediated within 30 days. Renewals require fresh justification.

Compensating controls examples
- If administrative read access is required temporarily, require session recording, heightened alerting, and daily attestations by approver.
- For delayed patching, require network isolation, WAF rules, and additional logging.

Metrics and reporting
- Number of open exceptions (target: 0 for critical controls).
- Average time to remediate approved exceptions (target: <30 days).
- Quarterly report to Executive Security Committee.

Appendices and references
- Related pages: Security Control Book, Incident Response Playbook, RBAC Implementation Guide, Data Residency Contract Templates.
- Tools: Okta (IdP), Vault (secrets), Splunk (security logs), Datadog (traces/metrics), AWS CloudTrail (cloud audit logs), KMS/HSM (key management).
- Templates: Access Request form, Exception Request template, Chain-of-Custody form, Audit Evidence manifest.

Contact and escalation
- Security oncall: security-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty)
- Compliance: compliance@redwood.com
- Emergency legal: legal@redwood.com
